response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remain, COUNT(*) AS exec_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE expirespot BETWEEN '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark) SELECT AVG(avg_remain) AS avg_of_order_avg_remaincount, SUM(exec_count) AS total_executions FROM per_order;

assumptions.assumption: expirespot is compared as text with BETWEEN, so both bounds are inclusive and the comparison is lexicographic, as the request specifies. This assumes stored values use the same 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS[.ffffff]' format; the schema declares expirespot as TEXT(6) while the documentation describes it as a TIMESTAMP.
AVG(remaincount) skips NULL values, so missing remaincount values are ignored within each order. An order whose remaincount values are all NULL gets a NULL average and is skipped by the outer AVG.
number of executions is COUNT(*), which counts every execution row for the order, including rows whose remaincount is NULL.
rows with a NULL ordersmark form one group and are included in the results. The request does not say whether unlinked executions should count.
no rounding is applied, so the averages and sums are returned at full precision.

alternatives.interpretation: Count only executions that have a remaincount value, so the execution count matches the rows that feed the average. Orders with no remaincount values contribute 0 to the total.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude executions with no linked order (NULL ordersmark) so that only real orders are grouped and counted.
